_comment: Model registry — the single source of truth for which inference models the
scanner can run under. Read by shared/models.ts (TypeScript stages) and by
run.sh / diff.sh / seed-upstream.sh (bash, via node), so the three can never
Adding a model is a data change, not a code change: append one entry to
`targets`. Nothing under tools/scanner/*/src/ needs to know it exists.
A target's KEY is also its run-artifact namespace: runs/<key>/<stage>/.
Key on the model, not the vendor — api.openai.com serves luna, terra and sol,
and each needs its own isolated run tree to be comparable.

luna.label: GPT-5.6 Luna
luna.notes: Long-context (>272K prompt) rates are 0.4/1.8 and are NOT modelled: the registry carries one rate pair, so a long-context run under-reports. GPT-5.x reasoning models reject max_tokens with a 400, and reject any temperature but the default, so steering happens through the prompt and through reasoning_effort. reasoning_effort was added 2026-07-31: runs 1-5 sent none at all and therefore ran at the endpoint's default, so four rounds of playbook work were tuned against the cheapest tier of the family at that tier's own cheapest effort. Re-measured 2026-08-01 on the 40-lane platform against a matched control: high effort alone is recall 53.6% -> 63.9%, 10 entries gained and 0 lost. Paired with Stage 2's default trace loop it is 67.0% recall and 85.6% localization, the shipped arm — see docs/run-history.md 2026-08-01 and docs/architecture/stage2-lane-loop.md. max_output_tokens must move with the effort: reasoning tokens are billed as output AND counted against the cap, and at this effort 42% of calls exceed 8000, where a truncated body is unparseable JSON that Stage 2 records as a lane that found nothing — measured recall 63.9% -> 37.1% at an 8000 cap. Raised 24000 -> 64000 on 2026-08-01. The 14584 figure was the highest completion on run 6's workload only; a deliberately output-maximising lane-shaped probe on the same model returned 29682 completion tokens, so 24000 truncates a harder-but-legitimate lane and the earlier claim that 16000 would do was wrong. 64000 is ~2.2x that measured worst case and half the model's 128000 hard ceiling (established by API rejection, not documentation). The cap is a ceiling, not a spend — billing is per token generated — so headroom is free, while a low cap truncates JSON into what Stage 2 records as a lane that found nothing. All six benchmark targets share 64000 so no cross-model comparison is confounded by differing room to answer. 'medium' is untested. To reproduce runs 1-5 exactly, set SCANNER_REASONING_EFFORT= and SCANNER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000 and HUNT_LOOP=none rather than editing this entry. base_url null means the SDK default, https://api.openai.com/v1. Requires api.openai.com on the environment's egress allowlist.

terra.label: GPT-5.6 Terra
terra.notes: Long-context rates are 4.0/18.0 and are not modelled. Middle tier of the GPT-5.6 family, same endpoint and key as luna. $2.50/$15 per MTok against luna's $1.00/$6.00. Added 2026-07-29 because every run to date has used the family's cheapest tier: docs/'Cybersecurity models pricing research' records luna as 'the smallest step up available' from qwen on cost grounds, so model capability has never been isolated as a variable.

sol.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
sol.notes: Long-context rates are 10.0/45.0 and are not modelled. Top tier of the GPT-5.6 family, same endpoint and key as luna. $5.00/$30 per MTok, ~5x luna on input. Rated 96.7% on OpenAI's internal CTF suite, which they describe as saturated — read it as 'not capability-limited on security reasoning', not as a percentage of anything. See the pricing research doc's caveats before treating that number as a ranking.

luna-fixed.label: GPT-5.6 Luna (post-fix arm)
luna-fixed.notes: Same model and same rates as luna. Same model as luna. A separate key so the run-5 artifacts in runs/luna/ stay untouched while the same model is re-measured with the 2026-07-29 fixes in force. Exists to separate 'the fixes helped' from 'the model tier helped' — without it, a terra-vs-run-5 delta confounds both. Experiment arm: do not merge to main.

qwen.label: Qwen 3.6 Plus
qwen.notes: DashScope's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Accepts only max_tokens. This was the default target before the registry existed; it is kept so the committed runs/qwen/ baseline stays reproducible. Deliberately unpriced: the vendor bills this model's output at two different rates depending on whether the request runs in thinking mode, and the registry carries one rate pair. A single number here would be wrong for one of the two modes, and pricingFor() returning null prints no cost rather than a wrong one.

qwen37.label: Qwen 3.7 Plus
qwen37.notes: The vendor advertises a limited-time 20% discount not applied here, so actual spend runs below projection until it lapses. The >256K tier is 1.2/4.8 and is not modelled. Added 2026-08-01. A separate target from `qwen` rather than a bump of it: `qwen` pins Qwen 3.6 Plus so the committed runs/qwen/ baseline stays reproducible, and reusing the key would silently repoint that baseline's namespace. Verified 2026-08-01 on the endpoint above: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured, temperature 0.1 accepted. Shares DASHSCOPE_API_KEY and QWEN_MODEL with `qwen` — setting QWEN_MODEL therefore overrides BOTH targets at once, which would silently collapse a 3.6-vs-3.7 comparison into one model. Leave it unset.

gemini36flash.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash
gemini36flash.price_tier: standard, flat-rate — the vendor publishes no context tier for this model
gemini36flash.notes: Added 2026-08-02. Reached through Google's OpenAI-compatibility layer, same endpoint and credential as gemini31pro, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. Output price includes thinking tokens. Cache storage ($1.00 per MTok-hour) is not modelled. Shares GEMINI_MODEL with gemini31pro, so setting that env var overrides BOTH targets at once and would collapse a pro-vs-flash comparison into one model — leave it unset. max_output_tokens 64000 matches the other benchmark targets so no model has less room to answer than another; it is not a measured ceiling for this model. Note gemini31pro was observed declining an exhaustive-enumeration task (862 output tokens where peers emitted 25k-31k); whether this model shares that behaviour is unmeasured, and it matters because recall is monotone in trace length.

gemini31pro.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
gemini31pro.notes: Output price includes thinking tokens. The >200K tier is 4.0/18.0 and is not modelled, so a lane whose prompt crosses 200K under-reports by ~50%. Added 2026-08-01. Reached through Google's OpenAI-compatibility layer, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change; the /v1beta/openai suffix on base_url is what selects that layer. The model id is gemini-3.1-pro-preview — the bare 'gemini-3.1-pro' 404s with NOT_FOUND. Verified 2026-08-01: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured. max_output_tokens is set high for the same reason as luna's and matters MORE here: a 16-token probe returned finish_reason 'length' with completion_tokens 0 and an empty body, because thinking consumed the entire budget before any content was emitted. Downstream that is indistinguishable from a lane that found nothing, so do not lower this cap without re-measuring. 24000 is inherited from luna's slack rather than measured on this model — the highest completion actually observed here is unknown.

glm52.label: GLM-5.2
glm52.notes: Cache storage is free for a limited period and is not modelled. Added 2026-08-01. Z.ai's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. Credential env var is ZAI_API_KEY, not a GLM_-prefixed name. Verified 2026-08-01: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured. A first attempt on 2026-08-01 returned HTTP 429 code 1113 'Insufficient balance' — auth had already succeeded at that point, so read a 1113 as an unfunded account rather than a bad key. The same model is also resold through DashScope at the same list price; this entry uses the vendor endpoint directly.

opus5.label: Claude Opus 5
opus5.price_tier: standard first-party API, global inference_geo, 5m cache writes
opus5.notes: The batch discount (50%) and the 1.1x us-only inference_geo multiplier are not modelled. Fast mode is 10/50 and is not used. Added 2026-08-01. VERIFIED 2026-08-01 via shared/preflight.ts: model id resolves, plain completion returns content with finish_reason=stop, and json_schema strict is honoured. Reached through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatibility layer at /v1/chat/completions, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. The credential var is SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: this runs inside Claude Code, whose harness strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the container (its own sessions authenticate through the account), so that name cannot carry a scanner credential here — it arrives unset no matter where it is configured, and the key had to come in through the environment's setup script. Same reason base_url_env is SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: the ambient ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set without the /v1 suffix and would resolve every call to a 404 path. max_output_tokens 24000 is inherited slack rather than a measured ceiling — no completion length has been observed on this target under a real stage prompt.

sonnet5.label: Claude Sonnet 5
sonnet5.price_tier: standard first-party API, global inference_geo, 5m cache writes, INTRODUCTORY
sonnet5.notes: INTRODUCTORY pricing, expires 2026-08-31. From 2026-09-01 the rate becomes 3.0/15.0 (cached 0.30, 5m write 3.75), a 50% increase that takes a full run from ~$43.88 to ~$65.83. Update this entry on that date or every later run under-reports by a third. Added 2026-08-01. VERIFIED 2026-08-01 via shared/preflight.ts: model id resolves, plain completion returns content with finish_reason=stop, and json_schema strict is honoured. Same transport and same credential handling as opus5 — see that entry for why the vars are SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Shares ANTHROPIC_MODEL with opus5, so setting that env var overrides both targets at once and would collapse an opus-vs-sonnet comparison into a single model. Leave it unset. max_output_tokens 24000 is inherited slack rather than a measured ceiling.
